# Results — Study 598 (Cederburg "100% Equities for Life")

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test
(Anarkulova, Cederburg & O'Doherty 2023) — **a lifecycle invested 100% in stocks, half
domestic / half international, beats stock/bond balanced strategies and target-date glidepaths
on retirement wealth AND ruin risk** — raced on monthly-start 70-year lifecycles (save 40
years, retire 30 years, 4% rule) on the Shiller 1871+ real-return tape plus an honest
international proxy. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-07-03** (run date); the cached Shiller extract's last
**complete full-data month is 2023-06** — no partial months are used. Fingerprint
`b68792bbdbe0`. Sibling of [151](../../151-stocks-for-long-run/) (the horizon claim — this
study is the **lifecycle allocation horse race**, not the horizon test) and
[596](../../596-bond-tent-glidepath/) (the decumulation glidepath shape).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | Shiller S&P 500 monthly (cache-first `_cache/shiller_sp500.parquet`) + iShares EFA monthly total return (yfinance, `_cache/efa_monthly.csv`) |
| Window | 1871-02 → 2023-06 (**1,829 months**); real US equity **+6.90%/yr**, real INTL **+3.91%/yr**, real BD **+2.39%/yr** (geometric, CPI-deflated) |
| International leg | **262/1,829 months (14.3%) are market data** (EFA, 2001-09 →); everything before is **LITERATURE-CALIBRATED, NOT market data** — deterministic seed-598 simulation at the DMS world-ex-US parameters (geo 4.3%/yr, vol 17%, corr 0.60 with US; realised pre-EFA corr 0.593, EFA-era market corr 0.627). Named on the Signal axis; a pure-tape domestic variant and a corr = 1 stress are always shown beside it |
| Bond leg | 10-year Treasury first-order approx (carry − 7 × Δy), **CPI-deflated** — every leg real; stated as a decision |
| Cohorts | **990** monthly-start **70-year lifecycles** (starts 1871-02 → 1953-07; retirements 1911-02 → 1993-07): contribute 1.0 real/yr for 40 years, then withdraw **4% of the pot at retirement**, fixed real, for 30 years; ruin = depleted before age 95 |
| Strategies | `alleq` 100% equity 50/50 dom/intl (the paper's pick); `alleq_dom` 100% domestic equity; `s6040` static 60/40; `tdf` glidepath 90% → 45% (at 65) → 30% equity (dom/intl 50/50) |
| Execution / costs | weights are a deterministic function of age, set at the end of the prior year (one clean lag; the only signal is the calendar); **10 bps one-way × traded value + 5 bps/yr expense ratio × NAV**, all strategies |

> **What is simulated and what is not.** The US equity and bond legs are market data
> (survivorship-free single-index series — the named bias is the opposite one: the US is the
> best equity market in recorded history, flattering every domestic-equity-heavy rule). The
> international leg is market data only from 2001-09; its first 130 years are a
> literature-calibrated simulation, because no public 150-year international monthly tape
> exists. Every conclusion that leans on the blended `alleq` is therefore cross-checked
> against `alleq_dom` (pure tape) and a corr = 1 stress that deletes the diversification
> benefit — the ordering below survives all three.

## Head-to-heads — HAC *t* (Newey-West, bandwidth = full 840-month overlap)

Per-cohort terminal-wealth differences at 4%; ruin gaps in percentage points; outer circular
block bootstrap (600 reps, 120-month blocks, seed 598) for tape-level 95% CIs.

| comparison | mean ΔTW | HAC *t* | boot 95% CI (ΔTW) | Δruin | boot CI (Δruin) | win rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **HEADLINE** alleq − 60/40 | +161.0 | **+1.22** | [−334.4, +1341.4] | **+2.22 pp** | [−14.95, +22.22] | 55.4% |
| **VS GLIDE** alleq − TDF | +260.7 | **+2.63** | [**+2.1**, +1891.0] | −13.13 pp | [−24.15, +14.55] | 88.2% |
| **PURE TAPE** alleq_dom − 60/40 | +369.9 | **+11.72** | [**+32.1**, +5170.1] | −1.41 pp | [−8.39, +9.70] | 94.7% |

Reading: the half of the claim aimed at **target-date glidepaths is real** — the all-equity
lifecycle beats the TDF on terminal wealth at HAC *t* = **+2.63** with a bootstrap CI that
excludes 0, and carries a −13 pp cohort ruin gap (not separately certified; CI wide). The half
aimed at **balanced 60/40 fails on this tape for the paper's own 50/50 blend**: *t* = +1.22,
CI straddles 0, the median race is a tie (203 vs 191) — and the blend's ruin is *worse*
(+2.22 pp; a single-draw point estimate — worse in 9/20 residual re-draws, see the
seed-robustness section). What *is* decisively certified is the **domestic** all-equity lifecycle
(*t* = +11.72, CI excludes 0) — but that is US-exceptionalism territory
([study 151](../../151-stocks-for-long-run/)), not the paper's diversified prescription. No
ruin-risk advantage is certified for any all-equity variant.

## Ruin rates by withdrawal rate (share of cohorts depleted before age 95)

| wr | alleq | alleq_dom | s6040 | tdf |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 3.0% | 0.10% | **0.00%** | **0.00%** | **0.00%** |
| 3.5% | 2.93% | 0.51% | **0.00%** | 0.51% |
| 4.0% | 7.98% | **4.34%** | 5.76% | 21.11% |
| 5.0% | 24.95% | **20.00%** | 25.96% | 51.21% |

At conservative withdrawal rates the blend is the *only* strategy that ever ruins; at 4–5% the
TDF is the disaster (its bond-heavy retirement years meet the CPI-deflated bond tape's
1940s–70s) and the domestic all-equity is safest — the paper's *"100% equities cuts ruin
risk"* holds against TDFs, **not** against a plain 60/40, and only via the domestic leg.

## The Cederburg machinery — 2,000 bootstrap lifetimes (120-month blocks, seed 598)

The paper's own method: resample 840-month lifetimes from the joint tape, all strategies on
identical draws. 4% rule:

| strategy | pot @65 (median) | terminal mean | terminal median | ruin |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| alleq | 153.0 | 577.3 | 290.6 | 9.55% |
| alleq_dom | 214.2 | 1433.7 | 660.8 | 6.95% |
| s6040 | 148.9 | 423.7 | 259.0 | **7.15%** |
| tdf | 129.2 | 172.3 | 95.5 | 13.70% |

The generative view agrees with the cohort panel: the blend's ruin (9.55%) is **not** lower
than 60/40's (7.15%). The paper's opposite finding rests on its 38-country return panel, where
*bond* returns are far worse than the US 10-year (+2.39%/yr real here) and international
equity is stronger — on a US-anchored tape with the DMS world-ex-US calibration, the
international half drags.

## Sensitivity — what the international-leg assumption does (alleq vs 60/40)

| pre-2001 INTL leg | ruin | mean TW | HAC *t* vs 60/40 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **hybrid (headline)** — DMS-calibrated + EFA | 7.98% | 350.6 | +1.22 |
| corr = 1 stress — zero pre-2001 diversification | 13.74% | 228.0 | +2.31 |
| domestic — INTL = US, pure tape, no simulation | 4.34% | 559.4 | +11.72 |

No assumption rescues the headline pair: the blend never beats 60/40 on ruin, and its wealth
edge is only certified in the degenerate variants that abandon the international leg's return
calibration. The claim's fate is decided by the **level of international returns**, not by the
correlation assumption.

## Seed-robustness — re-drawing the simulated INTL residuals (seeds 598–617)

The pre-2001 international leg is a seeded simulation, and single-seed verdicts are banned on
this desk — so both head-to-heads are re-run under 20 independent residual draws:

| comparison | HAC *t* mean | min | max | *t* ≥ 2 | verdict |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
| alleq − TDF | +6.58 | **+2.63** | +10.04 | **20/20** | ROBUST — the headline seed 598 is the *weakest* draw |
| alleq − 60/40 | +2.62 | **−16.54** | +10.76 | 13/20 | SIGN FLIPS — not decided by market data |

`ruin(alleq) > ruin(60/40)` in **9/20** seeds — the ruin race against 60/40 is a coin flip
across residual draws (matching the wide bootstrap CI [−14.95, +22.22]; the 7.98% vs 5.76%
point estimate is one draw of that coin). And on the **pure tape** (nothing simulated
anywhere): `alleq_dom − tdf_dom` mean ΔTW **+437.7**, HAC *t* = **+13.07**, ruin **4.34% vs
11.52%**. The certified all-equity-vs-TDF edge survives every residual draw *and* the pure
tape; nothing in the 60/40 race is decided by market data.

## Third axis — does 100% equities survive the worst historical cohorts?

Terminal wealth (× annual contribution) at 4%; `fy` = years into retirement at depletion
(−1 = survived).

| retire | alleq | alleq_dom | s6040 | tdf | alleq under corr = 1 stress |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1929-09** (crash) | **0.0 (fy 18)** | 0.0 (fy 18) | **62.0 (survived)** | 3.8 (survived) | 0.0 (fy 16) |
| **1966-01** (inflation grind) | **190.9 (survived)** | 0.0 (fy 25) | 0.0 (fy 25) | 0.0 (fy 27) | 0.0 (fy 20) |

**BUSTED.** The 1929 retiree is ruined by year 18 under *every* all-equity variant while the
60/40 finishes with 62× and even the TDF survives. The 1966 retiree survives under the blend
**only through the literature-calibrated international leg** — the pure-tape domestic variant
and the corr = 1 stress are both ruined, so the one historical rescue the strategy can claim
is delivered by the *simulated* half of the portfolio. On the actual market data the tape
contains, 100% equities does **not** survive the worst cohorts.

## Robustness — costs

| one-way / ER (bps) | alleq mean TW | alleq ruin | HAC *t* vs 60/40 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 / 0 | 364.9 | 7.98% | +1.21 |
| **10 / 5 (headline)** | 350.6 | 7.98% | +1.22 |
| 25 / 20 | 313.0 | 9.39% | +1.23 |

Costs are a non-factor for the verdict: two-index-fund lifecycles are among the cheapest
strategies that exist; the *t* barely moves across a 4× cost sweep.

## Synthetic control — the engine is faithful

20 independent seeded worlds per setting; detector = alleq vs 60/40, one-sample *t* across
worlds. Exact null: **premium = 0** (equal arithmetic means ⇒ equal expected terminal wealth
for every schedule), so the mean-wealth detector must read ~0 there. *(Machinery proof only —
never cited as market evidence.)*

| planted arithmetic equity premium | Δmean TW | *t* | Δruin | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0 pp (exact null)** | +3.2 | **+1.55** | +5.95 pp | +3.15 |
| 2 pp | +43.6 | +4.01 | +2.33 pp | +1.14 |
| 4.5 pp (historical) | +342.8 | **+4.92** | −0.23 pp | −0.14 |

The mean-wealth detector reads ~0 at the exact null and lights up with the planted premium;
the ruin detector exposes the risk channel — at a thin premium, 100% equity ruins *more* and
the gap closes as the premium grows. That is precisely the economics the real-tape verdict
turns on: the domestic leg's 4.5 pp premium certifies wealth dominance, the international
leg's ~2 pp premium does not.

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** Split, spelled out: **Real vs the TDF glidepath** — the 100%-equity
  lifecycle beats the target-date path on terminal wealth at HAC *t* = **+2.63** (bootstrap CI
  [+2.1, +1891] excludes 0) with a −13.1 pp cohort ruin gap (directional; CI wide). **Not
  certified vs plain 60/40 for the paper's own 50/50 dom/intl blend** — *t* = +1.22, CI
  straddles 0, median tie, and cohort ruin is *worse* at the headline draw (+2.22 pp; the
  Cederburg-style bootstrap agrees, 9.55% vs 7.15% — though across 20 residual re-draws the
  ruin race is a coin flip, 9/20: *no ruin ranking vs 60/40 is decided by the data*). The
  seed-robustness check certifies the TDF half under every draw (HAC *t* ≥ 2 in 20/20 seeds,
  the headline +2.63 being the weakest; pure-tape domestic race *t* = +13.07) while the 60/40
  wealth race flips sign across draws. The domestic-only variant *is* decisively certified
  (*t* = +11.72) but rides US exceptionalism, named here and graded as the horizon claim in
  study 151. Named on this axis: **85.7% of the international leg is literature-calibrated
  simulation, not market data** (parameters and seed stated; ordering survives the corr = 1
  and domestic variants).
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Nothing is cheaper or more accessible than a two-index-fund 100%
  equity lifecycle (the *t* is flat across a 0→25 bps cost sweep, capacity unlimited) — but
  the certified edge needs a **70-year horizon**, tolerates ruin in the single worst
  retirement cohort of the tape (1929), concentrates in US-exceptionalism, and the ruin-risk
  half of the pitch is uncertified everywhere. A real premium harvested through a vehicle
  whose safety claim did not replicate: FRAGILE, not INVESTABLE.
- **"Does it survive the worst historical cohorts (1929, 1966)?" — BUSTED.** The 1929 retiree
  is ruined under every all-equity variant (fy 16–18) while 60/40 survives with 62×; the 1966
  retiree is rescued only by the *simulated* international leg — the pure-tape variants are
  ruined. The strategy's worst-case story rests exactly on the data that does not exist.
